main_body: Two stacked logs lying on their sides, with round cut ends facing the viewer on the left and dark bark bodies running to the right
top_band: none: the column through the bark body goes from a thin lighter brown highlight (rows ~4-5) straight into dark bark. No horizontal surface is visible from above. The pale ellipses are vertical cut faces.
evidence: The logs are drawn as a side profile. The circular end grain and the long bark cylinders are vertical or curved faces seen from the side. Only a 1px highlight runs along the top of the bark, which is a rim and not a top surface. There is no top band, no front-edge line and no eave shadow. This matches the side-elevation failure in the guide.

style.evidence: The cut ends have a decent ramp: cream, tan and brown rings with a centre dot. The outline is a dark brown that suits the wood. The bark bodies, however, are broad areas of nearly flat dark brown with only a highlight line and a few grain marks, which is thinner than the textured stall and well references. The piece is small and has fewer colours per tile than the references. Because of the flat bark fills I fail it, being strict.
